title: Knowledge in the book
hookLine: the first word is read, and knowledge is praised throughout

cards: If you had to guess the first word of a holy book's revelation, you might guess pray, or believe, or obey.
In the Islamic account, the angel Jibril comes to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in a cave on Mount Hira, and the first word is none of those. It's iqra'. Read.
Or recite. Surah ninety-six, in Pickthall's translation: "Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth." A revelation whose first word is read.
From there, knowledge runs through the whole of it.

teach.b: The word is 'ilm, knowledge. Its root, '-l-m, gives a whole family: 'alim, one who knows; its plural, 'ulama', the scholars; mu'allim, a teacher; and al-'Alim, the All-Knowing, one of the names of Allah.
In al-Baqarah, the first human, Adam, is honored by being taught: Allah taught him the names of all things, and the angels admit they know only what they've been taught.

Surah thirty-nine asks a question that doesn't need answering: "Are those who know equal with those who know not?" In surah fifty-eight, Allah raises in degrees those who believe and those given knowledge.

And in surah twenty, the Prophet himself is told to ask for more of it: "My Lord! Increase me in knowledge." Some commentators note it's the only thing he is told to ask more of. The hadith carry it on.
One, in Ibn Majah, says seeking knowledge is a duty on every Muslim. Another, in Sahih Muslim, says whoever walks a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for them a path to the Garden.
And here's a line people repeat that isn't in the sources: seek knowledge even as far as China. It's often quoted, and hadith scholars judged it weak or invented.
Which is itself a lesson in 'ilm: knowing includes checking. Muslim scholars built a whole science around asking who said a thing, and whether it was really said.

how: Muslims treat seeking knowledge as a religious duty; some recite "my Lord, increase me in knowledge" (20:114) before study, and hadith scholarship developed careful methods for checking who transmitted a report.

games.q: in surah twenty, the Prophet is told to ask his Lord to increase him in one thing. what is it?
games.why: knowledge: my Lord, increase me in knowledge. some commentators note it's the only thing he's told to ask more of.

practice: Ask yourself: what's one thing I'd like to understand better? A word from this year's lessons, a skill, a question about someone you love.
Pick it and hold it, and if you pray, say the Prophet's line from surah twenty: my Lord, increase me in knowledge.

wordCard.voice: 'Ilm. Knowledge, from '-l-m, the root of scholar, teacher and the All-Knowing: what the Prophet is told to ask more of. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: knowledge. the same root gives 'alim, 'ulama' and al-'Alim.

carryVoice: Your line: seek knowledge. Read first, and check what you read. Day six hundred sixty-eight.
